claims.promise: The round, its visit history and the balances open and save with the phone in airplane mode and with no account, so nothing in the daily path waits on a login or on someone else's server being up.

evidence.finding: Yardbook, 4.6 stars over 100K+ installs, draws a 3-star review reading "Login hasn't worked in over a month. Always says incorrect password or Email, even when the exact same credentials work on browser", and LawnPro, 3.5 stars over 10K+ installs, draws a 1-star review reading "They did a server upgrade and it wasn't done correctly, took everything down without warning for about 3 days" plus another reading "They deleted all my clients payment information"; the account and offline classes together appear in 3 of the 8 critical operator-side reviews read.

proof.assertion: Run `node scripts/run-slot-tests.mjs --slot lawn-round-log --rerun`: the case saves a round through the on-device document store, reloads it and asserts the operator's order comes back identical, and `everyBalanceIsIdenticalAfterASaveAndLoadRoundTrip` does the same for the money. The store is a local file — `RoundStore.kt` opens no socket and the merged manifest declares zero permissions, so the round opens, records a visit and saves with the phone in airplane mode and no account created.

claims.promise: It is a recurring seasonal round rather than an appointment book: the day's customers are an ordered list he can reorder, one tap marks a visit mowed, skipped or rained-off, and a rained-off morning pushes the whole round by a day in one action.

evidence.finding: Missing-feature is 3 of the 8 critical operator-side reviews read (38 percent) and arises on a shelf whose operator apps are job and booking shaped, while 29 of 30 visible titles on the lawn care client tracker query are on the job and 13 of the 22 rated ones sit below 4.2 stars; the single-action rain push itself is not directly measured on this shelf.

proof.assertion: Run `node scripts/run-slot-tests.mjs --slot lawn-round-log --rerun`: the case advances a rained-off round by one day and asserts every still-due visit moved exactly once, and `aSecondPushFromTheSameDayMovesNobodyTwice` and `pushingTwiceInARowMovesEachCustomerExactlyTwoDaysWithoutDuplicatingAnyOfThem` assert the same day cannot be pushed twice. The ordered list is proved beside them by `theRoundKeepsTheOrderTheOperatorDrivesIt` and `movingTheBottomCustomerToSecondPlaceReordersTheRoundAndReflowsPositions`.

claims.promise: A per-customer running balance shows who still owes and for what, marked off in one tap when cash or a transfer arrives, without an accounting suite and without generating an invoice document.

evidence.finding: The paywall class is 3 of the 8 critical operator-side reviews read and the accuracy class 1 of 8, on operator tools whose money handling its users openly distrust, and LawnPro's 1-star review reports that clients payment information was deleted; what is owed is the fourth clause of this lane's own definition and no incumbent complaint measures the balance feature directly, which is why this claim is inferred rather than measured.

proof.assertion: Run `node scripts/run-slot-tests.mjs --slot lawn-round-log --rerun`: the case records two mowed visits at 40 each and a 40 payment against one customer and asserts the running balance is 40, matching a hand-computed total; `aPaymentIsRecordedOncePerDayAndANonPositiveAmountRemovesIt` proves the one-tap mark-off and its undo, and `owedByCustomerListsOnlyUnsettledCustomersInRoundOrder` proves the list is who still owes, in round order, with no invoice document. `theBalanceIsDerivedSoCorrectingTheVisitCorrectsTheMoneyWithoutATouchOnAnyBalanceField` proves the balance is derived rather than stored.

claims.promise: One price, no subscription, no advertising and no renewal prompt, so the operator is not renting access to his own round.

evidence.finding: LawnBook, 4.4 stars over 500+ installs, draws a 3-star review reading "80 dollars for a pretty-new app, for premium? that's kinda insane", and all 8 enriched lawn incumbents declare no advertising while only 3 declare any in-app purchase, so the shelf's money is rent rather than a one-time price.

proof.assertion: Read `ui/unlock/UnlockViewModel.kt`: the only paywall is `BillingPurchaseGate`, a one-product `PurchaseGate` over the billing capability's controller; `MainActivity.kt` builds it once and `PlayKilnApp.kt` gates the app on it. Its own contract states one product with no consumables and no subscriptions, and `res/values/strings.xml` tells the user `unlock_price_note` = "One payment. No subscription and no renewal." No renewal path exists anywhere in `app/src/main`.

claims.promise: Every control on the day list is reachable one-handed with a 48 dp target and stays legible in direct sunlight, because it is used standing at a curb with the mower running.

evidence.finding: The shelf's paying users are operators working outdoors rather than desk users, and no incumbent complaint on this shelf measures tap-target size or outdoor contrast, so the requirement is inferred from the job and stated here rather than presented as a measured finding.

proof.assertion: Read `ui/round/RoundScreen.kt`: the day list's controls are floored at 48 dp — the mark, move-up and move-down buttons each carry `.size(48.dp)` and the status action is `Modifier.widthIn(min = 48.dp)`; the same floor is repeated in `Brand.kt` (`heightIn(min = 48.dp)`) and every other screen. `node scripts/verify.mjs --slot lawn-round-log` independently reports `uiux.a11y`: 35 clickable elements, each with an accessible name and none with a declared extent below 48 dp. The sunlight half is the slot's own palette in `ui/theme/Color.kt`, whose light values are the ones `store/studio.json` declares and are chosen for an outdoor screen rather than for a desk.
